description.narrative: The project supports the Government of the Philippines in implementing and expanding its social protection agenda, especially the conditional cash transfer (CCT) program Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (Pantawid) and the Listahanan national household targeting system for poverty reduction (NHTS-PR). The associated TAs will support capacity development and institutional strengthening of the government for efficient implementation of the social protection agenda.

description.narrative: Original Project: Increased consumption and utilization of education and health services among poor households and women beneficiaries of 4Ps Overall Project: Household consumption and the use of education and health services by Pantawid families (especially mothers and children) are increased

By 2019 (nationwide unless otherwise noted): At least 70% of pregnant women deliver in a health facility (2008 baseline: 44.5%) Achievement: 83.77 Progress/Status: Exceeded target. The IE3 confirms that 83.77% of pregnant women delivered in a health facility Data Source: NSCB small area estimates of poverty; Impact evaluation survey (DSWD); MIS (DSWD); Proxy means test (DSWD); Data published by NSCB; National demographic and health survey (NSO); Field health service information system; APIS

By 2019 (nationwide unless otherwise noted): At least 90% each of boys and girls age 3-18 in Pantawid families attend school (2013 baselines: 63% age 3-5, 97% age 6-14, and 60% age 15-18) attend school Achievement: 95.7 Progress/Status: Exceeded target for monitored beneficiaries (based on period 6 ((December 2019-January 2020), prior to the implementation of enhanced community quarantine due to COVID-19 pandemic). a. Monitored Beneficiaries The average compliance rate of children 3-18 years old is 95.7%. 3-5 years old:97.2% (Boys - 97.0%; Girls - 97.3%) 6-14 years old:96.5% (Boys - 95.5%; Girls - 97.6%) 15-18 years old:94.1% (Boys - 92.5%; Girls - 95.8%) 3-18 years old:95.7% (Boys - 94.5%; Girls - 96.9%)
b. Eligible Beneficiaries The average compliance rate of children 3-18 years old is 81.6%. 3-5 years old:91.4% (Boys - 91.1%; Girls - 91.7%) 6-14 years old:87.4% (Boys - 85.8%; Girls - 89.1%) 15-18 years old:72.0% (Boys - 68.9%; Girls - 75.3%) 3-18 years old:81.6% (Boys - 79.4%; Girls - 83.9%)
All program conditions are suspended for Period 1 to 4 2020 (February to September 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The approval of the conditions' suspension is based on RA 11310 Section 15 of Rule VIII. Data Source: NSCB small area estimates of poverty; Impact evaluation survey (DSWD); MIS (DSWD); Proxy means test (DSWD); Data published by NSCB; National demographic and health survey (NSO); Field health service information system; APIS

By 2019 (nationwide unless otherwise noted): At least 80% of births are delivered by skilled health personnel (2008 baseline: 62.2%) Achievement: 85.21 Progress/Status: Exceeded target. IE3 results confirm that 85.21% of births were delivered by skilled health personnel. Over time, there has been a shift from midwife-assisted to doctor-assisted deliveries for beneficiary mothers. Difference in urban/rural results highlights the still limited access to doctors in rural areas as compared to that in urban areas. This also points to supply-side issues that need to be addressed for the program to achieve desired impact. Data Source: NSCB small area estimates of poverty; Impact evaluation survey (DSWD); MIS (DSWD); Proxy means test (DSWD); Data published by NSCB; National demographic and health survey (NSO); Field health service information system; APIS

By 2019 (nationwide unless otherwise noted): At least 85% of children are fully immunized before 1 year old (2008 baseline: 70%) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Based on the IE3, among children at least 1 year old to 5 years old, preliminary data shows no impact on the full immunization rate which remains at 70%. The IE3 also found no impact of the incidence of vaccine-preventable diseases. This is consistent with the persistent finding in the previous evaluations that the 4Ps does not increase the proportion of children who received complete immunization by age one. The program will continue education of participants to increase immunization. Data Source: NSCB small area estimates of poverty; Impact evaluation survey (DSWD); MIS (DSWD); Proxy means test (DSWD); Data published by NSCB; National demographic and health survey (NSO); Field health service information system; APIS

By 2019 (nationwide unless otherwise noted): At least 10% increase in average per capita consumption of beneficiaries in target communities Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: ADB analysis of the 3rd Impact Evaluation (IE3) data shows that per capita household income increases by 61% when the value of grants is included in household income, but without grants no significant change to per capita income is detected. This increase in household income translates to an 8% increase in total household consumption with clothing, school supplies, healthcare, and food showing significant increase which indicates more investment in the welfare of the families. IE3 key findings indicate that the program: (i) still continues to deliver on its objectives of improving the health and education of children from poor households; (ii) increased school participation of children, particularly those in age cohorts at higher risk of dropping out; (iii) increased utilization of key health care services and interventions for children and pregnant women; and (iv) HHs had large expenditure share on health, clothing and footwear compared to non-beneficiaries households; and, the program does not encourage dependency nor does not it increase expenditures on vice goods such as tobacco, alcohol, and gambling. Data Source: NSCB small area estimates of poverty; Impact evaluation survey (DSWD); MIS (DSWD); Proxy means test (DSWD); Data published by NSCB; National demographic and health survey (NSO); Field health service information system; APIS Baseline value: $211

By 2019 (nationwide unless otherwise noted): Decrease in the share of children 6-14 years old who are working (2008 baseline: 4.6%). Achievement: N Progress/Status: The IE3 shows that 90% of the children aged 10 to 14 years, who are in employment, continue to be enrolled in school. The IE3 did not collect information on children aged 6 to 9 years old. However, no significant difference was observed for beneficiary versus non-beneficiary households in terms of incidence of child labor and time spent on child labor. Data Source: NSCB small area estimates of poverty; Impact evaluation survey (DSWD); MIS (DSWD); Proxy means test (DSWD); Data published by NSCB; National demographic and health survey (NSO); Field health service information system; APIS Base year: 2008 Baseline value: N

As of July 28, 2020, the second tranche pay-out is still on-going wherein 1,335,711 of the 1,361,034 (98.1%) cash card holders already received their ECA as of that time. The beneficiaries for second tranche are only those residing in the areas specified in the Executive Order No. 112, S. of 2020 dated April 30, 2020 and the Memorandum issued by Executive Secretary Salvador Medialdea on May 2, 2020 as well as other related resolutions issued by the Inter-agency Task Force on Emerging Infectious Diseases (Region III except Aurora Province, National Capital Region, Region IV-A, provinces of Benguet, Pangasinan, Iloilo, Cebu Province, Albay Province, and cities of Bacolod, Davao, and Zamboanga City).
